headline: Explicit probabilistic models resolve cell-state and spatial heterogeneity in transcriptomic data
label: Probabilistic Models Of Cell Heterogeneity
summary: Mixture and Bayesian models now partition cells, spots and RNA localization with uncertainty, alongside spatial testing and benchmarking frameworks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit probabilistic structure for resolving heterogeneity in single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. PHM-ensemble pools ensemble mixture density estimates for multiresolution clustering of 1.82M immune cells, and ELLA-mix uses a finite mixture with a count-conditioned Poisson framework to find subpopulations with distinct radial RNA localization. SCATTER deconvolves spots into cell-type proportions and per-type expression, while SpaDAG learns spatially varying causal DAGs with MCMC. ACE-OF-Clust aligns and compares mixed-membership solutions. Downstream, spatialFDA and STAVAG add formal testing of co-localization and of directionally and temporally variable genes, and a 15-method benchmark evaluates tissue alignment. Newer here is the pairing of model-based partitioning with inference that is spatially and condition-aware. Not every item uses mixture models; several supply testing or evaluation infrastructure.
